text:
rachel: hey, new to infra — merged the portal kubeconfig into my ~/.kube/config and now `kubectl config get-contexts` shows duplicate names. I tried `kubectl use-context redwood-dev` but it pointed at prod. how do i safely fix without risking prod?

tom: welcome! easiest fix: stop using the merged file. move ~/.kube/config -> ~/.kube/config.bak and put portal yaml into ~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml. then `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml:~/.kube/config.bak`

rachel: hmm okay. i already ran a few reads but no writes. is there a quick way to confirm my current context's API server so i can be sure?

tom: `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` shows api server. if it contains `prod` in the hostname don't run writes. Also `kubectl auth can-i create deployment -n team-rachel` tells you write perms.

devex-bot: Docs: https://docs.internal/redwood/onboarding/k8s#safe-kubeconfig. Tip: rename conflicting contexts with `kubectl config rename-context <old> <new> --kubeconfig=FILE` on a copy.

rachel: ok i renamed the context in a copy and set KUBECONFIG. now `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-rachel` -> Forbidden. i filed portal ticket ONB-540. is that normal?

sre: yes, new hires are given namespace-scoped view role via a temporary RoleBinding. we can fast-track if you paste your user string: `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].name}'`
rachel: output: rachel@redwood

sre: created RoleBinding `rb-onboard-rachel` in `team-rachel` binding `view` to `rachel@redwood`, expires in 72h. try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-rachel` then `kubectl get pods -n team-rachel`.
rachel: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-rachel` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-rachel` shows 2 pods. thanks! :tada:

onboarding-bot: Reminder: temporary access expires in 72 hours (ONB-540). To extend, reopen ticket with justification and PR links if applicable.

rachel: quick question — when should I ask for a service account instead of a user binding?

sre: SAs are for automation (CI jobs, tools). For interactive work we use your SSO identity. if you need long-lived programmatic access we'll create a namespaced SA and rotate tokens per policy.

tom: also recommend installing `kubectx` and `kubens`, and adding aliases like: `alias kteam="KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml kubectl --context=redwood-dev-rachel"` to avoid mistakes.

rachel: will do. closing this thread — thanks everyone for the quick help!
